assessment: This is an important paper that shows most cancers unavoidably accumulate damaging mutations. Whilst the majority of claims are convincingly supported by the data, evidence that damaging changes are buffered by heat shock pathways is currently incomplete. The insights into selection efficiency are important for the understanding of cancer growth and response to therapy. A broader implication is that high mutation load tumors may use common strategies to tolerate accumulated deleterious mutations, providing a therapeutic target.
